correctness.rationale: Exact outer-node force equations yield sin u=sin v; complementary solutions have negative weighted-Laplacian trace and cannot be attracting. On the symmetric branch the two explicit Jacobian eigenvalues, strictly concave torque, and unique maximizing phase prove the iff threshold and uniqueness. The implicit-function calculation proves strict monotonicity and exact 2^{-p} asymptotic coefficients. A separately executed standalone finite checker replays 52 direct Jacobian spectra and 15 asymptotic cases; it does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: An exact finite-exponent all-weighted-triangle branch and its competing coherence and spectral-gap asymptotics are not stated or implied by the motivating many-oscillator work or the examined finite-size uniform-coupling papers. Published generic budget lower bounds are explicitly treated as prior, not new. Limited full-text access to one uniform-coupling source remains a historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: Full text of Xin–Kikkawa–Liu (2016) was not available; its publisher abstract specifies only uniform coupling. This restricts the confidence of exact historical-priority assessment.
The frequency-weighted network literature is broad; a comprehensive independent priority examination is still needed.
Finite sample spectral checks are corroborative, not exhaustive and not independent scientific validation.

value.rationale: A practically motivated cost-constrained edge allocation has a complete nontrivial smallest-network transition: increased p simultaneously improves stationary phase coherence and destroys the slow transverse spectral gap, with matching exact geometric rates. This reveals a concrete design tradeoff invisible from coherence-only optimization and is neither the already-known budget lower bound nor a routine textbook substitution.
